mainTopic: When a husband can annul his wife's נזירות, and a father's power to make his son a נזיר
overview: The amud opens by explaining a dispute in the previous משנה about when a husband loses the power to annul his wife's נזירות. The תנא קמא says it is once the blood is sprinkled, because from then on she may drink wine and no longer suffers. רבי עקיבא says it is once an animal is slaughtered, because annulling would cause הפסד קדשים. רבי זירא challenges this with a ברייתא about the כבשי עצרת: the blood could be sprinkled שלא לשמה, and then the meat would still be eaten. The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא is speaking of a case where the חטאת was slaughtered first, and a חטאת cannot be saved that way. The משנה then limits the whole rule to a תגלחת טהרה. רבי מאיר says the husband may annul even then, because he does not want a shaven wife; the two sides disagree over whether a wig solves the problem. A new משנה teaches that a father can make his young son a נזיר but a mother cannot, and explains what happens to the son's animals and money if the נזירות is cancelled. The גמרא asks why only a father has this power. רבי יוחנן answers that it is a special הלכה for נזיר, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The reasoning of the first opinion in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of our משנה holds that once the blood is sprinkled she may drink wine right away. Her vow no longer causes her suffering, so the husband cannot annul it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our תנא holds: once the blood was sprinkled for her, she may drink wine right away, so she no longer suffers from the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תנא קמא says the husband can no longer annul once the blood has been sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband can only annul vows that cause his wife suffering or distress. Once the blood of her offering is sprinkled, her נזירות is basically over and wine is permitted immediately. There is nothing left to annul, because the vow no longer hurts her.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא of our משנה (the first, unnamed opinion)
the blood was sprinkled on the מזבח
immediately
being downcast or disgraced; suffering from the vow

phrases.english: The tanna of our Mishnah holds:
Once the blood has been sprinkled on her behalf,
she is immediately permitted to drink wine,
and so she is not downcast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the משנה's dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the blood is sprinkled, wine is permitted immediately, so there is no suffering left to annul.

steps.title: The reasoning of רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that as soon as one animal is slaughtered, the husband cannot annul, because annulling would waste sacred property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds: even once just an animal was slaughtered, he cannot annul, because that would cause a loss of sacred property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא cuts off the husband's power even earlier, at the slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the blood is sprinkled, she still cannot drink wine, so she is still suffering. רבי עקיבא's reason is a different one. If the vow were annulled after the animal was slaughtered, the slaughtered קרבן would no longer be needed and would go to waste.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal was slaughtered
to annul a vow
loss or waste of sacred property

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds:
Even if just an animal was slaughtered,
he cannot annul,
because of the loss of consecrated property.

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא's reason is that she is no longer suffering. רבי עקיבא's reason is that annulling would cause הפסד קדשים.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the dispute, based on a different reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once an animal is slaughtered, annulment is blocked because of הפסד קדשים.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks why there would be any loss
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks why there would be a loss. The כהן could just sprinkle the blood שלא לשמה, and then the meat could still be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objects: Why? Let him sprinkle their blood not for their proper purpose, and the meat will be permitted to eat!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רבי עקיבא's reason of הפסד קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vow is annulled, the slaughtered animal cannot count as a נזירות offering anymore. But it could still be offered as an ordinary קרבן by sprinkling its blood שלא לשמה. Then the meat is eaten and nothing is wasted, so רבי עקיבא's worry seems to disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenges it
and why?
not for their proper intended purpose

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objects to this:
And why?
Let him sprinkle their blood not for their own sake,
and he will permit the meat to be eaten!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's reason from step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reason of הפסד קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The loss can be avoided by sprinkling the blood שלא לשמה, which still lets the meat be eaten.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the שבועות lambs
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא backs up his challenge with a ברייתא. If the כבשי עצרת were slaughtered for the wrong purpose or at the wrong time, the blood is still sprinkled and the meat is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it taught: The lambs of שבועות that were slaughtered not for their purpose, or before or after their time, the blood is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a source showing that we sprinkle blood שלא לשמה just to save the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כבשי עצרת, slaughtered wrongly, can no longer serve as the שבועות offering. Even so, the ברייתא says to sprinkle the blood so the meat can be eaten. The same should be done for the נזירות offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
the two communal שלמים lambs of שבועות
before their proper time

phrases.english: Isn't it taught:
The lambs of Shavuot that one slaughtered not for their own sake,
phrases.notes: עצרת is the גמרא's name for שבועות.

phrases.english: or that he slaughtered before their time
or after their time,
the blood shall be sprinkled and the meat shall be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's challenge with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That we sprinkle blood שלא לשמה in order to save the meat

steps.title: The ברייתא continues with a שבת case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that on שבת the blood is not sprinkled. If it was sprinkled anyway, the offering is accepted and the אימורין are burned that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was שבת, the blood should not be sprinkled. But if he did sprinkle it, it is accepted, and the אימורין are burned in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a side case about שבת. Its weekday ruling still shows that sprinkling שלא לשמה is done on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling these lambs does not push aside שבת, so on שבת we start out by not doing it. Even so, if it was done, it still works, and the fats wait until nightfall. On a regular day the sprinkling is done right from the start, which is רבי זירא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: it was accepted; the offering is valid
to burn on the מזבח
the parts of the animal burned on the מזבח
in the evening, after שבת

phrases.english: And if it was Shabbat, it should not be sprinkled.
And if he did sprinkle, it is accepted,
to burn the sacrificial parts in the evening!

steps.confusionAlert: The שבת rule is only a side detail of the ברייתא. רבי זירא's proof comes from the main ruling: on an ordinary day, we sprinkle the blood שלא לשמה from the start so the meat can be eaten.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא brought as proof
steps.raayaObject: That sprinkling שלא לשמה is a normal way to save the offering
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rest of the same ברייתא

steps.title: רבי עקיבא is talking about a slaughtered חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The answer agrees with רבי זירא for a עולה or שלמים. It explains that רבי עקיבא means a case where the חטאת was slaughtered first.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: If he slaughtered a עולה or שלמים, that is true. But what case are we dealing with here? Where he slaughtered the חטאת first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי זירא by limiting רבי עקיבא's ruling to a case where the חטאת was slaughtered first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a עולה or שלמים, sprinkling שלא לשמה would save the animal, so annulling causes no loss. A חטאת offered שלא לשמה is not valid, so it cannot be saved this way. That is where רבי עקיבא's concern about הפסד קדשים is real.

keyTerms.meaning: they say (an answer from the חכמים)
so too; indeed, that is correct
what case are we dealing with here?
first

phrases.english: They say:
If he slaughtered a burnt-offering or a peace-offering,
so too.
phrases.notes: In other words, you're right: in that case we'd sprinkle שלא לשמה, and the husband could still annul.

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
Where he slaughtered the sin-offering first.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's rule that the husband cannot annul once an animal is slaughtered applies when the חטאת was slaughtered first. A חטאת cannot be rescued by sprinkling שלא לשמה.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אִי דִּשְׁחַט עוֹלָה אוֹ שְׁלָמִים הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from steps 3 to 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's concern of הפסד קדשים seemed avoidable for any offering by sprinkling שלא לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא speaks of a slaughtered חטאת, which cannot be saved by sprinkling שלא לשמה, so there would be a real loss.

steps.title: Proof that the חטאת can be brought first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if the נזיר shaved after bringing any one of his three offerings, he has fulfilled his duty. This shows the חטאת may come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If he shaved after bringing one of the three offerings, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a source for the answer in Step 6. A נזיר's חטאת can really be slaughtered first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 explained that רבי עקיבא is talking about a case where the חטאת was slaughtered first. This משנה proves that case can happen. Shaving after any one of the three offerings counts, so the order is flexible, and the חטאת can be the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
He shaved (the נזיר's hair at the end of his נזירות)
He has fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: As we learned: If he shaved
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in the מסכתא (45a).

phrases.english: after one of the three of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: The three are the נזיר's עולה, שלמים and חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 6 by showing the חטאת can be offered first.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי עקיבא's case is one where the חטאת was slaughtered first.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (נזיר 45a): shaving after any one of the three offerings is valid.

steps.title: The husband cannot annul at a pure shaving, but can at an impure one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the earlier rule. The husband loses the ability to annul only at a shaving of purity. At a shaving of impurity he may still annul.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? At a pure shaving. But at an impure shaving, he may annul (because he can say: I do not want a disgusting wife).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה. It quotes the line that limits when the husband loses his power to annul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the husband cannot annul once her offerings are underway (after the blood is sprinkled, or for רבי עקיבא, once an animal is slaughtered) applies only to תגלחת טהרה, the shaving at the end of a completed נזירות. At תגלחת טומאה, the shaving after the נזיר became impure, he can still annul.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? (a limit on the earlier rule)
The shaving at the end of a pure, completed נזירות
The shaving a נזיר does after becoming impure
He may annul (the vow)

steps.confusionAlert: The words in round brackets explain why the husband may annul at an impure shaving. Many versions leave them out, so do not build the whole משנה on them.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: He means the earlier rule that the husband can't annul once her offerings are underway.

phrases.english: At a shaving of purity.
But at a shaving of impurity, he may annul
(because he can say:
phrases.notes: Many versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: I do not want a disgusting wife).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and limits its rule (Steps 1-2) to a pure shaving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband cannot annul only at a תגלחת טהרה. At a תגלחת טומאה he can.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: he may annul even at a pure shaving
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees. The husband may annul even at a pure shaving, because he can say he does not want a shaven wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Even at a pure shaving he may annul, because he can say: I do not want a shaven wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי מאיר's opposing view. The husband can always annul at the shaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the issue is not wasting sacred property. It is the husband's own interest in his wife's appearance. Her shaving affects him personally, so he keeps the right to annul.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with the first opinion
I do not want
A woman with a shaven head

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר says:
Even at a shaving of purity, he may annul,
because he can say:
I do not want a shaven wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to the rule in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband may annul even at a תגלחת טהרה, since he does not want a shaven wife.

steps.title: The תנא קמא's reply: she can wear a wig
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the תנא קמא answers רבי מאיר. The wife can wear a wig, so the husband has no real complaint.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא would tell you: It is possible with a wig.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the reasoning behind the dispute. First it shows why the תנא קמא is not bothered by רבי מאיר's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said the husband would be stuck with a shaven wife. The תנא קמא answers that a wig solves the problem. So the shaving does not really harm the husband, and his right to annul is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
A wig (literally, 'foreign hair')

phrases.english: And the first תנא would say to you:
It is possible with a wig.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the first opinion answers רבי מאיר's argument from Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical solution that removes the husband's complaint
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A shaven wife would really harm the husband, so he should be able to annul.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wig solves it, so the תנא קמא sees no harm at a pure shaving.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a wig is dirty, so it is no solution
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rejects the wig solution. A wig is dirty, and the husband does not want it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר holds: As for a wig, since it is dirty, he is not happy with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי מאיר's side. A wig does not fix the problem, so the husband keeps his right to annul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole dispute comes down to one point: is a wig an acceptable fix? The תנא קמא says yes. רבי מאיר says no, because a wig is dirty and a husband would not accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
Dirt, filth
He is not happy with it; it does not suit him

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and רבי מאיר disagree about whether a wig solves the husband's problem with a shaven wife. That decides whether he can annul at a pure shaving.

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר holds:
As for a wig,
since it is dirty, he is not happy with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wig solution offered for the תנא קמא in Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the wig as a solution, not the תנא קמא's whole position.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A wig is dirty, so the husband would not accept it.

steps.title: New משנה: a father can make his son a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a father can make his young son a נזיר, but a mother cannot. The son or his relatives can cancel it by shaving or by objecting.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man can make his son a נזיר, but a woman cannot make her son a נזיר. How so? If the son shaved, or his relatives shaved him, or he objected, or his relatives objected.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה begins on a new topic. A father has the power to vow נזירות for his young son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This special power belongs only to the father, not the mother. The משנה then lists ways the son's נזירות can be ended: the son shaves, his relatives shave him, he objects, or his relatives object for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Makes someone else take on a vow
His relatives
He objected, protested

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new topic: the special rule that a father can place נזירות on his son. It also starts listing what cancels it, and the גמרא will discuss this next.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A man can impose a vow
of נזירות on his son,
phrases.notes: He means a son who is still a minor.

phrases.english: but a woman cannot impose a vow
of נזירות on her son.
How so?
If he shaved, or his relatives shaved him.
If he objected, or his relatives objected.
phrases.notes: In any of these cases, the son's נזירות is cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִישׁ מַדִּיר אֶת בְּנוֹ בְּנָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on an unrelated topic after the wife's-vow discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father can impose נזירות on his minor son, but a mother cannot. Shaving or objecting by the son or his relatives cancels it.

steps.title: What to do with animals already set aside
steps.stepSummary: If the son had animals set aside for his נזיר offerings, the חטאת is left to die, the עולה is offered as an עולה, and the שלמים are offered as שלמים. The שלמים are eaten for one day only and need no bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had an animal set aside: the sin-offering must die, the burnt-offering is offered as a burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings are offered as peace-offerings. They are eaten for one day, and they do not need bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the case from Step 12. It tells us what happens to animals the son already set aside before his נזירות was cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal is handled differently. The חטאת cannot be offered, so it is left to die. The עולה and שלמים are still offered, but the שלמים keep some of the rules of a נזיר's שלמים: they are eaten for only one day. They lose one rule, though, because they do not need the loaves that usually come with them.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal set aside for a specific offering
Sin-offering
Burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Peace-offering, eaten by the owners
It must die (it is left to die, not offered)

phrases.english: If he had an animal set aside,
phrases.notes: "He" is the son whose נזירות was just cancelled in the earlier part of the משנה.

phrases.english: the sin-offering must die,
and the burnt-offering is offered as a burnt-offering.
And the peace-offerings are offered as peace-offerings,
and they are eaten for one day,
and they do not require bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from Step 12 and works out what happens after the son's נזירות is cancelled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separated animals: the חטאת dies, the עולה is offered as an עולה, and the שלמים are offered as שלמים, eaten for one day, without bread.

steps.title: What to do with money already set aside
steps.stepSummary: Unspecified money goes to communal gift offerings. Money set aside specifically for the חטאת is thrown into ים המלח. Money for the עולה buys an עולה, and money for the שלמים buys שלמים, which are eaten for one day without bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had unspecified money, it goes to gift offerings. If the money was specified: the sin-offering money goes to the Dead Sea; one may not benefit from it, but there is no liability for misuse. With the burnt-offering money they bring a burnt-offering, and there is liability for misuse. With the peace-offering money they bring peace-offerings, eaten for one day, without bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now covers money instead of animals. It tells us what to do with coins the son set aside for his offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is whether the money was labeled. Unlabeled money goes to נדבה, gift offerings for everyone. Labeled money follows its label: חטאת money is destroyed, while עולה and שלמים money is used for those offerings. With חטאת money there is no liability for מעילה, but with עולה money there is.

keyTerms.meaning: Unspecified money, not assigned to a particular offering
Specified money, assigned to a particular offering
Voluntary gift offerings
The Dead Sea, where the money is thrown so no one uses it
Liable for מעילה, misusing holy property

steps.whatToRemember: Unlabeled money goes to gift offerings. Labeled money follows its label: חטאת money is destroyed, and עולה and שלמים money is used for those offerings.

phrases.english: If he had unspecified money,
it goes to gift offerings.
If the money was specified:
the money for the sin-offering goes to the Dead Sea,
one may not benefit from it, but there is no liability for misuse.
With the money for the burnt-offering they bring a burnt-offering,
and there is liability for misuse of it,
with the money for the peace-offerings they bring peace-offerings,
and they are eaten for one day,
and they do not require bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from animals already set aside to money already set aside, still in the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unspecified money goes to נדבה. Specified חטאת money goes to ים המלח with no מעילה. Specified עולה money buys an עולה and carries מעילה. Specified שלמים money buys שלמים, eaten for one day, without bread.

steps.title: Why a father but not a mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by restating the משנה's rule that a man can make his son a נזיר but a woman cannot, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A man, yes, but a woman, no. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion. It quotes the rule from Step 12 that only a father can make his son a נזיר, and asks why. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives this power to a father and denies it to a mother without saying why, so the difference needs an explanation. The גמרא wants to know where this father-only rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
No
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Gemara:
A man, yes,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה's rule that a father can make his son a נזיר.

phrases.english: but a woman, no.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rule taught in Step 12 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a father can make his son a נזיר but a mother cannot.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a special law for נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that this is a הלכה, a received law given specifically for נזיר. The גמרא then begins to introduce a second answer from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is a received law regarding a נזיר. And רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. He says the father-only rule is a special tradition just for נזיר. The גמרא then starts to bring a second opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not give a logical reason or a פסוק. He says it is a received law, which many understand as a הלכה למשה מסיני. Because it is a special rule for נזיר, it applies only to a father and does not need to make sense from ordinary logic. The last words open רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view, which continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A received law, a tradition rather than something learned from a פסוק
A person who takes a vow to avoid wine, haircuts, and impurity from the dead
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
An אמורא who gives a second answer

steps.whyThisMatters: Calling it a special הלכה for נזיר keeps this father-only power limited to נזיר. It does not become a general rule about vows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is a received law regarding a nazir.
And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina...

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הֲלָכָה הִיא בְּנָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15, then begins a second answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יוחנן, the father's power to make his son a נזיר is a special received law (הלכה) for נזיר.
